clue.text: Bury getting new doctor

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

explanation.surface: A doctor is being buried, or a funeral is given a fresh medic.

explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a junior hospital doctor in training, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: American suspect not tried before the public

clue.text: Method in pureeing the quince

clue.text: More personal attention from the providers of the Gideon Bible?

definitions.text: More personal attention from the providers of the Gideon Bible?

parts.words: More personal attention from the providers of the Gideon Bible?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the Bible-placing Gideons might offer a more personal ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gideons are an evangelical society that places free Bibles in hotel bedrooms; the clue pretends they deliver to each room the way hotel staff deliver food.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel staff bringing food and drink to a guest's bedroom is the personal attention the phrase names.

clue.text: Creator of statue — see reverse, covered in tumbling curls

explanation.walkthrough: 'see reverse' is the note at a page foot telling the reader to turn over, abbreviated; 'tumbling' jumbles the curls and 'covered in' wraps them round that note.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor is the artist who carves or models statues.

clue.text: Place indeed for cooking cake ingredient?

clue.text: Officer's position: head of unit, soldier supporting quite a few

ant is the crossword soldier, from the soldier ants of a colony

explanation.surface: An army officer's rank: in charge of a unit, his soldiers backing several others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts the soldier ANT beneath TEN in this down entry; the soldier ant is a standard crossword soldier.

clue.text: In this bone a chip inhibits one getting up

clue.text: Man longing to come up to bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' reverses YEN to NEY, set below ROD in the down entry; 'Man' is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodney is a male first name, so a man may be called that.

clue.text: Country's leader retaining memory for now

rote is memory work, learning by heart

explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' signals the container; learning by rote is learning from memory, and the country's leader is its Prime Minister, not its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem, Latin pro tempore, means temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Atom-smasher: limits of capacity, control slipping

explanation.definitionFit: A cyclotron is a particle accelerator that drives charged particles round a spiral path, used to split nuclei.

clue.text: Fix editor to receive award

indicators.note: to receive means to take something in, so the editor's letters enclose the award

parts.note: the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for a newspaper editor to be given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' signals the container; the award is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly in a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Concern applied to flexing exercise? That's very surprising

parts.note: to mind is to concern yourself with or care about something
bending is the flexing movement of an exercise such as knee bends

explanation.surface: A remark about a stretching routine that turns out to be astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mind-bending is so strange or startling it is hard to take in.

clue.text: What's displayed as pretties out of gear?

definitions.text: What's displayed as pretties out of gear?

indicators.note: out of gear suggests mechanism thrown into disorder, so the letters of the words before it are scrambled; it also means out of clothing

explanation.surface: Pretty things put on show once the clothes come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of gear' works twice: it rearranges AS PRETTIES, and in the whole-clue reading it means undressed, which is the act itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is an erotic act in which a performer removes clothing piece by piece to show the body.

clue.text: I'd upset non-believer making analysis

explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I'D upwards to DI in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnostic is a test or analysis that identifies a fault or disease.

clue.text: Service provided for those who are late?

definitions.text: Service provided for those who are late?

parts.note: late can mean dead, the late Mr Smith, so the service is a church rite for the dead, not one for latecomers

explanation.surface: A church laying on an extra service for stragglers who missed the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy but means deceased here.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic Mass said for the souls of the dead is named from its opening word, Latin for rest.

clue.text: River of French blocked by one with a point

a means one, as in a single item

explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked by' signals the container: the French word is stopped up by the one with a point, so 'River of French' is not a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is Europe's second-longest river, flowing from Germany to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Arab about to perish following ship's officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container round the word for perish, and 'following' sets the result after the ship; 'ship's officer' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: See 15 across
See 5 down
Check I'd set about in car: nothing missing
